e. Allowing Hemp to Grow to Maturity (abandoning the project). There would be no immediate change in the environment. However, those individuals who pick the marijuana plants will be subject to arrest and it is estimated that 200 persons will be arrested. Thousands of pounds of marijuana will be picked and used. There will be an effect upon the internal environment of the individual using marijuana and since thousands of pounds will be available, some individuals may be involved as not only users, but sellers. By allowing the plant to grow to maturity and to be picked, the national policy of discouraging the availability and use of marijuana would be frustrated.
V. The Relationship Between Local Short-Term Uses of Man's Environment and the Maintenance and Enhancement of Long-Term Productivity
The elimination of the marijuana fields will have the beneficial effect of reducing marijuana use by decreasing the availability of the plant.

Law enforcement efforts could then be directed to other areas of concern.

The adverse impact of a transient influx of approximately 2,000 people into this farm community would be eliminated.
VI. Irreversible and Irretrievable Commitment of Resources
This program will cause no known irreversible or irretrievable commitment of resources.
VII. Description of All Planning to Be Taken to Minimize Any Unavoidable Adverse Environmental Effects
The loss of cover and feed will be overcome by reseeding of the area with appropriate cover this year.
